question: Should this repository accept Gmail Pub/Sub pull delivery as the first-party RFC direction, with pull staged through gog/OpenClaw/downstream implementation slices and push preserved as compatibility?
rationale: The patch is coherent RFC text, but accepting it sets cross-repo product direction and a future compatibility-sensitive default path that automation cannot decide.

options.title: Accept With Lifecycle Update
options.body: Accept the direction, create or link the implementation tracker, update the RFC from draft, and then merge the RFC.

options.title: Revise The Boundary
options.body: Request edits if maintainers want a different owner split, rollout sequence, proof gate, or push-compatibility policy.

options.title: Reject Or Pause
options.body: Keep the RFC unmerged if Gmail Pub/Sub pull should not become first-party OpenClaw direction yet.

recommendation.title: Accept With Lifecycle Update
recommendation.body: Accept the direction, create or link the implementation tracker, update the RFC from draft, and then merge the RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current RFC lifecycle policy that controls accepted-vs-draft merge handling.
